questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city and the culture. Great city and an opportunity to study at the worlds oldest university wasn't bad either.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find on the website. But, beware that when onlading, it is pivotal to look at the accessible time-slots.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some . It was okay to check in. But do research it beforehand.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It seems that the worlds oldest university is a bi antiquated.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is good to be out early.

Many websites do exist. But, there may be scammers. Never accept anything unless they have asked for your codice fiscale and alwasy ask for registration. If there is any hesitation, do not send any money. If it is to good to be true, it is. AirBnb can also be used. It is Italia. People are often more than willing to negotiate.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is somewhat expensive, but manageable. Avoid Casallechio. And try to find other people going down there. It may help bring down costs. >Anything more than 30 min on foot from piazza maggiore is a bit far away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It is quite straight forward. You just arrange a teams meeting when you have arrived.
But it is only avaliable in quite small timeslots. So be early. That is important.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only teams meetings. That is a bit problematic, but perserver.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not very.
Unlike other universities, UNIBO refuses to post advanced planning on their website before Aug. So first in august is it possible to see which courses may become avaliable.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take classes where you can avoid exams. Often times it is either written assignments or small quizzes you can take instead. Much easier.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If you are on the bachelor, it is very hard to get in to master programmes unlike UCPH. This may be very frustrating given the level of the bachelor courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Old school. Avoid Proff. Franzoni whose style is very antiquated. Many spoke english ineptly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CORPORATE FINANCE 9 ECTS.
PUBLIC ECONOMICS 8 ECS
POLITICAL BEHAVIOR AND INSTITUTIONS 10 ECTS
STRATEGY, BEHAVIOR AND POLICY IN ECONOMICS 8 ECTS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
POLITICAL BEHAVIOR AND INSTITUTIONS 10 ECTS
STRATEGY, BEHAVIOR AND POLICY IN ECONOMICS 8 ECTS

these two courses are great. They are very informative and offer good, thorough perspectives on the subjects they are about.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you by a bike, it may get stolen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks was very cheap given the level it is on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It hasn't got that much of a life. 
But, take italian classes. Those are great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Language classes and sports. But you need a doctor's note for sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Language classes to get a deeper cultural understanding of la civilta italiana.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the different cities like Parma, Modena, Reggio Emilia, Florence, Padova, Ravenna, or Verona. These are all very cheap to go to by train and takes like 1.5 hour.
You can also go father away.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's Italy. It is very easy. Get a negroni and settle right in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are nice and friendly. Just go talking with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Sometimes everything is a bit slow. But that's it.

Sometimes there is a language barrier. But, you can get quite far if you buy a danish-italian book on KUA.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The slowness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Seek grants because housing is expensiive. Look at the courses you want to take primo august. Explore Emilia-Romagna and Italy - it is called il belpaese due to a reason.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need a codice fiscale from the italian embassy. You have to be a bit pushy. They are very italian at the embassy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring Italy and the many new friendships I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was tackling being away at first. But you get used to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
